newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Hong Kong firm wins power plant deal in Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong firm wins power plant deal in Bangladesh.

text.p: Wartsila Power Development of Hong Kong has won a deal to set up a 100-megawatt barge-mounted power plant in Bangladesh's southern Khulna district, government officials said on Sunday.
Bangladesh's state-owned Power Development Board (PDB) and the Hong Kong firm on Saturday signed a 15-year agreement for operation of the plant, expected to be commissioned in 10 months.
The plant is expected to cost more than $90 million, they said.
The officials said the firm would sell electricity to PDB initially at the rate of 2.24 taka (5.1 cents) per kilowatt hour using imported furnace oil as fuel.
Two similar deals were signed last month, one with Smith Cogeneration of the United States and the another with a consortium led by U.S. firm Enron International.
Smith will set up a 130-megawatt plant in southwestern Chittagong while the Enron-led consortium will build a 100-megawatt plant near the capital, Dhaka.
PDB officials said more than 15 international firms participated in bidding on January 30 for the three barge-mounted power plants.
Bangladesh faces a severe power shortage. The country generates only 1,850 megawatts against demand of 2,200 megawatts.
Officials said Bangladesh was seeking overseas investment to raise power generation to 3,100 megawatts by the year 2000.
They said Saturday's deal brought foreign private investment in Bangladesh's power sector to about $400 million.
